---
title: Questions and answers
---

## Which formats does a handbook have?

A reading site and downloadable PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown and sources. Older releases may offer
fewer formats; each card shows what its release provides.

## Can an AI tool read a handbook?

Current-toolkit releases include one Markdown file with the whole book. [llms.txt](llms.txt) lists
every handbook and its Markdown edition.

## What does verified release mean?

Published files are downloaded and compared with the manifest and checksums. The reading site is
compared with the released HTML before a book is listed.

## Who decides what is listed?

The owner approves every catalog change after independent review. Authors keep control of their
repositories.

## Under which license are books published?

Content defaults to CC BY-SA 4.0 and code to MIT. Each book states its license and third-party notices.

## Does the hub host my manuscript?

No. Your repository holds the manuscript and releases; the hub stores the approved-release entry.

## What does it cost?

Nothing. The platform uses public repositories, their release pages and static sites.
